name: Introduction and overview — F-14 Tomcat — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — F-14 Tomcat
description: Introduction and overview of the F-14 Tomcat: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history. The F-14 Tomcat is a twin-engine carrier-based interceptor built by Grumman, entering U.S. Navy service in 1974. Its variable-sweep wings and long-range AIM-54 Phoenix missiles with the AWG-9 radar made it the fleet's outer air-defense fighter. 712 were built; the type was retired by the U.S. Navy in 2006 and continues only in Iranian service. Baseline facts: Twin-engine carrier interceptor; USN service 1974-2006; 712 built by Grumman; variable-sweep wings..
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
key_points: F-14 Tomcat: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history.
Twin-engine carrier interceptor; USN service 1974-2006; 712 built by Grumman; variable-sweep wings.
